content.title: Server Data, Persistence, and Synchronization
content.hook: Now consider the state that does not truly belong to the browser.
content.context:
Suppose a user profile comes from the server.

The browser may display it.

But the browser is not the authoritative owner of the profile.

That distinction changes how you design state.
goals: Master Server Data, Persistence, and Synchronization: unsaved user intent.

activities.title: Server data is not ordinary local state

content.title: Server data is not ordinary local state
content.text:
Consider:

```text
Server
  ↓
profile data
  ↓
application
  ↓
components
```

If you copy the profile into many unrelated local states, you now have several copies of remote truth.

That creates synchronization work.

content.question:
The server says:

```json
{
  "name": "Amina",
  "plan": "pro"
}
```

A component wants to show the name.

Should it create:

```js
const [name, setName] = useState(profile.name);
```

just to display it?

options.text: Only when the name is longer than ten characters

feedback.correct: If the component is simply displaying the current server value, copying it into local state can create a second source of truth.
feedback.incorrect: If the component is simply displaying the current server value, copying it into local state can create a second source of truth.

content.title: When local state is valid
content.text:
Suppose the user is editing the profile name before saving.

Now two values can legitimately exist:

```text
saved server name
draft name
```

The draft is not another copy pretending to be the source of truth.

It is a different concept:

**unsaved user intent.**

content.title: Persistence
content.text:
Some client state should survive refreshes.

Examples:

- a dismissed notice,
- a selected preference,
- a draft,
- a theme choice.

But persistence adds a new question:

**What happens when stored data is old?**

activities.title: Local storage is not the server

content.title: Local storage is not the server
content.text:
If you save:

```js
localStorage.setItem("theme", "dark");
```

that value exists in the browser.

It does not automatically update the server.

Likewise, a server update does not automatically rewrite every browser's local copy.

content.title: Synchronization is a product decision
content.text:
Imagine a user changes an account setting on one device.

Another device may have an old value.

Now the application must decide:

- which source wins,
- how often to refresh,
- when cached data becomes stale,
- whether the user should see a conflict,
- whether the change is optimistic or confirmed.

content.question: Which pair represents two different concepts?

options.text: Server profile and an identical duplicate state variable used only for display
URL query and the same query copied into four components
Derived total and another state variable containing the same total

feedback.correct: Correct answer: A. Server profile and unsaved draft
feedback.incorrect: Correct answer: A. Server profile and unsaved draft
